topics.title: Variables
topics.description: Variables are used to store data values. In JavaScript, you can declare variables using let, const, or var.
topics.example:
let name = 'Alice';
const age = 25;

topics.title: Number Methods
topics.description: JavaScript provides built-in methods to work with numbers, such as toFixed(), toString(), parseInt(), and parseFloat().
topics.example:
let num = 3.1415;
console.log(num.toFixed(2)); // 3.14

topics.title: String Methods
topics.description: Strings have many useful methods: slice(), substring(), toUpperCase(), toLowerCase(), includes(), and template literals using backticks.
topics.example:
let text = 'Hello';
console.log(`${text} World!`); // Hello World!

topics.title: Ternary & Logical Operators
topics.description: The ternary operator condition ? expr1 : expr2 is a shorthand for if-else. Logical operators &&, ||, ?? (nullish coalescing) are used for conditional evaluation.
topics.example:
let access = isAdmin ? 'allowed' : 'denied';
let name = userName ?? 'Guest';

topics.title: Switch Case
topics.description: The switch statement is used to perform different actions based on different conditions. Useful for replacing multiple if-else statements.

topics.title: Loops
topics.description: Loops are used to repeat code: for, while, do...while. Useful for iterating over arrays or performing repeated tasks.

topics.title: Type Conversions
topics.description: JavaScript can implicitly or explicitly convert data types. Functions like Number(), String(), and Boolean() are used for explicit conversion.
topics.example:
let x = '5';
let num = Number(x); // 5

topics.title: Strict Comparison
topics.description: Use === and !== for strict comparison to avoid implicit type coercion. == performs type conversion before comparison.
topics.example:
console.log(5 === '5'); // false
console.log(5 == '5'); // true

topics.title: Let, Var, Const
topics.description: Variables declared with var are function-scoped and can be hoisted. let and const are block-scoped. const cannot be reassigned.

topics.title: Hoisting & Temporal Dead Zone
topics.description: Hoisting moves variable and function declarations to the top of their scope. Variables declared with let and const are in the Temporal Dead Zone until initialized.
topics.example:
console.log(a); // ReferenceError
let a = 5;

topics.title: Functions
topics.description: Functions are reusable blocks of code that can take parameters and return values. Can be declared as function declarations, function expressions, or arrow functions.

topics.title: Scope
topics.description: Scope defines where variables are accessible. Global scope is accessible anywhere, function scope is accessible only inside the function, and block scope is accessible inside a block ({...}) with let/const.

topics.title: Closures
topics.description: Closures are functions that remember the variables from the scope where they were created, even after that scope has finished executing.

topics.title: Context & this
topics.description: The value of this depends on how a function is called. Methods, constructors, and arrow functions behave differently regarding this.
topics.example:
const obj = { a: 10, show() { console.log(this.a); } };
obj.show(); // 10

topics.title: Call, Apply, Bind
topics.description: Methods call, apply, and bind allow manually setting this for a function and optionally passing arguments.

topics.title: Default Parameters & Rest
topics.description: Functions can have default parameter values. The rest parameter ...args collects remaining arguments into an array.

topics.title: Spread Operator
topics.description: The spread operator ... allows expanding arrays or objects, e.g., merging arrays, copying arrays, passing arguments to functions.

topics.title: Destructuring
topics.description: Destructuring allows extracting values from arrays or objects into variables in a concise way.
topics.example:
const [a, b] = [1, 2];
const {name, age} = {name: 'Alice', age: 25};

topics.title: Object Methods
topics.description: Objects have methods like Object.keys(), Object.values(), and Object.entries(). Can also define getters, setters, and static methods.
topics.example:
const obj = { a: 1, b: 2 };
console.log(Object.keys(obj)); // ['a','b']

topics.title: Array Methods
topics.description: Arrays provide built-in methods for iteration, filtering, mapping, sorting, and flattening, such as map(), filter(), reduce(), sort().
topics.example:
const arr = [1,2,3];
const squares = arr.map(x => x*x); // [1,4,9]

topics.title: DOM Basics
topics.description: The Document Object Model (DOM) represents the HTML structure of a webpage. You can access and modify elements using document.getElementById(), querySelector(), etc.
topics.example:
const el = document.getElementById('title');
el.textContent = 'Hello World!';

topics.title: Events
topics.description: Events are actions in the browser, like clicks or keypresses. Use addEventListener to react to events.
topics.example: button.addEventListener('click', () => console.log('Clicked!'));

topics.title: Event Propagation
topics.description: Events propagate through three phases: capturing, target, and bubbling. You can stop propagation with stopPropagation() and prevent default behavior with preventDefault().
topics.example: form.addEventListener('submit', e => e.preventDefault());

topics.title: Timers
topics.description: JavaScript provides setTimeout() and setInterval() for delayed and repeated execution. Use clearTimeout() or clearInterval() to stop them.
topics.example:
const timer = setTimeout(() => console.log('Hello'), 1000);
clearTimeout(timer);

topics.title: Web Storage
topics.description: LocalStorage and SessionStorage allow storing key-value data in the browser. Cookies are another mechanism for persistent data.
topics.example:
localStorage.setItem('name', 'Alice');
console.log(localStorage.getItem('name'));

topics.title: Constructor Functions
topics.description: Constructor functions are used to create multiple objects with similar properties and methods using the new keyword.
topics.example:
function Person(name, age) { this.name = name; this.age = age; }
const alice = new Person('Alice', 25);

topics.title: Classes
topics.description: ES6 classes are syntactic sugar over constructor functions. Can define constructors, methods, and use extends for inheritance.

topics.title: Prototypal Inheritance
topics.description: Objects can inherit properties and methods from other objects via the prototype chain. Use Object.create() or __proto__.

topics.title: Promises & Async/Await
topics.description: Promises represent asynchronous operations. async/await syntax allows writing asynchronous code in a synchronous style.

topics.title: Error Handling
topics.description: Use try..catch to handle errors. Can also throw custom errors with throw.
